title: Cloud Load Balancing, Cloud CDN, and Cloud Armor — Failure Injection & Auto-Healing
purpose: Simulates volumetric Layer 7 DDoS attack: demonstrates Cloud Armor rate-limiting rules detecting malicious IP floods and dropping packets at the edge.
routing_rationale: Cloud Armor filters millions of malicious requests per second at Google's edge, preventing upstream application servers from suffering CPU or memory exhaustion.

nodes.label: Botnet HTTP Flood
nodes.detail: Distributed malicious nodes hammering /api/login endpoint with randomized headers.

nodes.label: Cloud Armor Rate Limiter
nodes.detail: Monitors per-client request frequency; flags clients breaching 100 req/min threshold.

nodes.label: Edge Drop Engine (GFE)
nodes.detail: Drops malicious TCP sockets directly at edge PoPs; returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.

nodes.label: Healthy Application Origin
nodes.detail: Origin backend servers remain at 12% CPU, serving legitimate users seamlessly.

steps.title: Attack Influx
steps.action: Botnet opens 100,000 HTTP requests per second across worldwide Anycast PoPs.
steps.why_traversal: Anycast distributes the attack across hundreds of Google edge facilities.

steps.title: Edge Rate-Limiting
steps.action: Cloud Armor rate limiting triggers immediately, rejecting attacking IPs with HTTP 429.
steps.why_traversal: Filtering happens in Google edge silicon; zero malicious packets reach backends.

steps.title: Protected Operations
steps.action: Clean customer transactions pass through unharmed; origin backends operate normally.
steps.why_traversal: Maintains 99.99% availability during severe volumetric cyber attacks.

scenarios.label: NAT Gateway False Positive Block
scenarios.root_cause: Rate limit rule grouped all enterprise corporate office users behind a single egress IP.
scenarios.diverted_path: Legitimate corporate employees blocked by Cloud Armor threshold.
scenarios.blast_radius: All employees on corporate WiFi receive HTTP 429.
scenarios.recovery: Configure Cloud Armor rate limiting based on Session Cookie or User-Agent instead of raw IP.

scenarios.label: Quota exhausted
scenarios.root_cause: A project or regional quota reaches its allocation limit.
scenarios.diverted_path: Requests surface elevated latency, errors, or denied actions.
scenarios.blast_radius: Consumers of the affected resource or dependency.
scenarios.recovery: Reduce load, restore the dependency, and add a tested prevention.

scenarios.label: Dependency unavailable
scenarios.root_cause: A required API or downstream dependency is unavailable.
scenarios.diverted_path: Requests surface elevated latency, errors, or denied actions.
scenarios.blast_radius: Consumers of the affected resource or dependency.
scenarios.recovery: Reduce load, restore the dependency, and add a tested prevention.

summary: Simulates volumetric Layer 7 DDoS attack: demonstrates Cloud Armor rate-limiting rules detecting malicious IP floods and dropping packets at the edge.
